chapter_theme: The unworthy recipient (அபாத்திரம்): a gift to those without discipline, vow and love of the Lord is wasted, like milking a barren cow or a crop sown out of season, and can drag giver and receiver alike to hell; given to the Lord, the pure guru and the desireless, it saves even a great sinner.
structure_note: Two verses on the waste of giving to the unworthy (505, 506), one on the right recipients (507) and one on the penalty of giving to those who do not revere the Lord (508).

505.reading: Giving to those without good conduct and vows is like stooping to feed fodder to a handsome barren cow and milking it for something to drink; it is a crop whose season has passed.
505.nuance: Two images of wasted effort: the barren cow (வறட்டு) gives nothing however well fed, and the late crop yields nothing however well sown. சீலம் and நோன்பு are taken as conduct and religious vows; the verse judges the recipient, not the gift.

506.reading: Know it as a great fault to give to anyone except those who know how to keep to yoga, yama and niyama and in whom love dwells, and not to those in whom love does not dwell though they know what profits.
506.nuance: ஈவது in line 1 can also be read as what is given: the teaching of yoga, yama and niyama is to be given only to those fit for it. On that reading the verse is about initiation rather than alms. Lines 2 and 3 repeat அறிந்து அன்பு தங்கு with a negation, which makes the contrast hard to fix.

507.reading: Even one who does not know the way and has done the five great sins, if he gives to the Lord, to the pure guru and to those who have left desire behind and has them teach him, will not enter the hell where such people go, but will learn true knowledge.
507.nuance: This is the reading in which புகான் (he will not enter) governs the whole: right giving outweighs even the five great sins (பஞ்ச பாதகம்). தரல்தந்து கற்பிப்போன் is compressed; it may instead mean one who gives and then presumes to teach such people, who goes to hell, but போதம் கற்கவே (so as to learn knowledge) fits the first reading better.

508.reading: Though one gives great wealth as large as a mountain of earth, if it goes to those who do not bow with joined palms, thinking 'this is the Lord', giver and receiver both reach the pit of the seventh hell.
508.nuance: ஏழா நரகம் is the seventh, lowest hell. The verse makes the giver share the fault: wealth is no excuse for an unworthy choice of recipient.

links.note: The converse case: the Naladiyar's small gift that reaches the hands of the worthy grows like a banyan seed until the sky looks small; Tirumular's gift to the undisciplined is a crop sown after its season. Both make the recipient's worth decide the gift's fruit.

250 tells the giver to give to everyone and not ask who they are; 506 calls giving to those without discipline and love a great fault. The two conflict if 506's ஈவது means giving in general; if it means imparting yoga teaching, they speak of different gifts.

The Kural defines true giving as giving to those who have nothing, all else being a loan expecting return; Tirumular judges the recipient by discipline and love, not by need. The conflict holds on the reading of 506 as about material giving.

507 says that even one guilty of the five great sins, if he gives to the Lord, the pure guru and those who have left desire, will not enter hell. 508 says that even wealth as large as a mountain, given to those who do not bow 'அண்ணல் இவன்' as to the Lord, sends 'ஈந்த இருவரும்', giver and receiver both, to the seventh hell. Read together, the recipient outweighs both the giver's sin and the size of the gift.

501 says gold the size of a sesame seed given to a knower of Siva bears fruit, while gold the size of the earth ('நிலமத்தனை பொன்') given to fools loses it. 508 says that even 'மண்மலை அத்தனை மாதனம்', great wealth as large as a mountain, given to those who do not bow to the Lord, sends both to hell. The chapter on the worthy recipient opens, and the chapter on the unworthy closes, on the same measure of earth-sized wealth; 508 adds that the giver himself is harmed.

source_issues: 508 line 3: இறைஞ்சாதார்ககு, a misprint for இறைஞ்சாதார்க்கு.
506 ends with a doubled full stop.
